pr_title: Add support for windows 10 mutiple windows and fix various tab/window related bugs
pr_body:
Fixes #509 
Fixes #1089

There is some changes in there that I'm not sure follow your intended behaviors for the application. Let me know if there's anything you want changed or that i'm simply misunderstanding.
pr_comments: Would also love this. Just started using Terminus in Win10 with WSL2 and would really love to be able to have multiple instances going across multiple Desktops spaces.

issue_context.title: Support multiple windows in Windows 10
issue_context.body: When I right click on the taskbar icon and click `Terminus` then nothing happens. Note that https://github.com/Eugeny/terminus/issues/170 does work. I can use `Ctrl + Shift + N`

review_comments: Any reason for this? The process needs to exit quickly after sending the second-instance message

Looking at all documentation for app.requestSingleInstanceLock() everything said to use app.quit(). app.quit() calls beforeunload and unload event handlers before exiting. Doesn't look like any of those handlers are in use right now but they may be added in the future.

I just felt that the process.exit(0) was redundant after calling app.quit().

I couldn't find much documentation on calling process.exit in an electron application other than `process.exit is a Node API, so I would assume that it may not do all the right things with regard to an Electron application.`

I'll happily add it in if app.quit() isn't enough!
Maybe app.exit(0) is a good solution?

Not necessarily. Take for example either running from CLI or starting with a shortcut

`Terminus.exe --debug open "C:\all-the-stuff"`

Here we'd see argv[1] be `--debug`. But if we use yargs.parse and look at `._[]` we will see the first "command" that was used.
